note: Senior Agbero's four attacks and his fight-stance bounce, cut from a 209-frame take. Art faces RIGHT, like every other Agbero sheet. Frame 0 of this sheet and frame 0 of senior-agbero-fall are the SAME guard drawing to the pixel (x[152..581] y[26..565]), which is what `bodyFrame: 0` on both anchors the scale to — the swap between attacking and being hit cannot pop.

sections.name: Guard
sections.description: The neutral. Not played as a clip — it is the scale anchor (bodyFrame 0) and the pose every other clip departs from and returns to.

sections.name: Jab
sections.description: ONE PUNCH out of a seven-punch flurry. The artist's 48-frame 'SeniorAgberoJab' section is a whole combination — ink reaches x1 833, 829, 827, 803, 811, 825, 871 in seven separate peaks — and binding all of it to one attack would give him a five-second unbreakable string. This is the first punch only: 61-62 chamber, 63 extends, 64-65 are full reach (x1 833), 66-67 retract. 0.23s, his fastest and safest move. The other six peaks are left on the cutting-room floor deliberately; if he ever needs a combination it is already drawn.

sections.name: Low Kick
sections.description: Mid-range pressure. 120 is the extension (x1 809) and 121-122 hold it; 123 onward folds it back. Lower than the high kick by a clear margin — compare the leg height in 120 against 36 — which is what makes it the move that goes UNDER a guard and has to be jumped rather than blocked.

sections.name: High Kick
sections.description: Committed, and cut to READ as committed. The source spends frames 0-27 barely moving — a 0.93s hold at 30fps that is the artist's idle padding, not a wind-up — so the clip starts at 28 where he actually loads. 30-33 is the leg up at head height (ink y0 drops to 10), 36 is maximum reach (x1 763), 37-40 recover. The tell lives in the move table's `windup`, not in replaying dead frames.

sections.name: Spin Kick
sections.description: His signature. The rotation is the tell: 45 is the narrowest point (x span 293) as he turns through, then 47 throws the leg out to x1 861 — the furthest reach of any move he has, ginger or senior. A spin is the clip that suffers most from dropped frames, because a rotation with gaps in it reads as a teleport rather than a turn — every frame ships.

sections.name: Ginger
sections.description: The fight-stance bounce — his default pose whenever Darki is anywhere near him, so it is the clip the player sees MOST, which is exactly why it now ships WHOLE. It used to be 129-141 ping-ponged: 13 of the artist's 45 emote frames, an 0.8s loop that came round often enough to read as a twitch rather than as a man shifting his weight. The full FightEmote section is 129-173 and every frame of it is the same continuous bob — checked on the art, not on the section name. PING-PONGED rather than cut as a loop, and that is the whole trick: he DRIFTS sideways across the performance (x0 wanders from 204 to 338 and on past 128), so no contiguous range returns to its own first frame. Playing up to 173 and back down to 130 returns to 129 by construction, so the seam cannot pop no matter how far he drifted. Same inverse trick the player's jump fall uses. 88 steps at the source rate, 2.93s a cycle — nearly four times the old loop, so the repeat stops being visible.
